name: Choose a pilot username before entering the galaxy
covers: custom pilot name shown in multiplayer identity
description: Verifies a player must enter a valid display name before joining the live galaxy and that the chosen name is retained.
steps: Try to enter with fewer than three characters
Enter a valid username such as StarRider and submit
Observe the pilot identity in the multiplayer panel
expected: Invalid short names are rejected; a valid chosen name starts the game and replaces the generated pilot name.

name: Pilot ships synchronize between two live players
covers: larger bright remote jet and visible username label
description: Verifies two pilots can join the shared galaxy and see each other's larger, labelled ships moving live.
steps: Actor A joins with username StarRider
Actor B joins in a second browser session with username NovaPilot
Move Actor B's ship and observe its enlarged jet and username label in Actor A's scene
expected: Both named pilots appear in the shared galaxy; each remote jet is visibly larger and easier to spot, and movement updates live.

name: Explore nine Solar System destinations
covers: Mercury Venus Earth Mars Jupiter Saturn Uranus Neptune and Pluto destinations
description: Verifies all nine named destinations are available to select and navigate toward.
steps: Select each of the nine destinations, including Pluto
Navigate toward Pluto and approach its surface
expected: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto are listed and Pluto can be approached and landed on.

name: Asteroid fields block the ship while the galaxy remains visible
covers: spiral galaxy star cloud and nebula effects
solid asteroid collision and speed impact
description: Verifies the Void contains visible cosmic scenery and asteroids that physically stop the ship.
steps: Fly forward through the asteroid route
Approach a visible asteroid and attempt to pass through it
expected: Stars and a distant spiral galaxy remain visible; asteroid rocks visibly obstruct the ship, trigger impact feedback and require a course change.

name: Keep mobile controls and planetary exploration intact
covers: mobile touch steering and altitude controls
description: Verifies the updated Solar System still supports touch flight and surface exploration on mobile.
steps: Select Earth and navigate close enough to descend
Use ASCEND and DESCEND to explore the surface
Launch back to space and observe the pilot presence indicator
expected: Touch controls remain usable, planetary landing and launch work, and multiplayer presence remains visible.
